attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own post, stated in his own voice.

semantics.note: Firm 'will' with the explicit 'at its current rate of construction' antecedent kept. Horizon 'late 2027' is preserved. Scored as a forecast, not hedged.

contract.note: The evaluator set Oct–Dec 2027 as 'late 2027' and chose the original eight-building campus. Both are ordinary readings. Requiring evidence that the rate held is strict but keeps the speaker's condition.

reviews.rationale: The forecast window ends 2027-12-31, after the 2026-10-28 evaluation date. The packet has no admitted evidence items and no dated completion event that meets the early-resolution rule. Whether the antecedent holds is unknown. The claim cannot be scored yet.

attribution.note: Zitron's own assertion in his own post.

semantics.note: 'Won't be built before, at this rate, 2030' is a firm forecast with a rate condition, and both are preserved. The scope (all deals or some) is not enumerated; the drafter's 'announced' wording is a slight gloss.

contract.note: The project set, the baseline rate and the completion unit are evaluator-supplied. Contradiction by any single completed in-scope facility is a strict reading of an ambiguous plural, but it is bounded by the rate condition. The deadline of 2029-12-31 is reasonable.

evidence.note: Crusoe's Sept 2025 release says two Abilene buildings were energized before the post. This is pre-publication, a company disclosure, and not a completion event.
Crusoe's June 2026 update: two buildings operational and six under construction. Partial progress only; it does not establish the rate condition or completion.

reviews.rationale: The deadline (end of 2029) is after the evaluation date. The evidence shows only partial progress at Abilene and no completion record for an identified in-scope project. The rate antecedent is not established. No conclusive early event, so the claim is not scored yet.

attribution.note: Zitron's own inference, drawn from his own earlier spending estimates.

semantics.note: 'Heavily suggests' signals strong confidence, not a medium/low hedge, so it is treated as a firm claim about current demand. The drafter's modality 'likely' understates it slightly. 'Pretty weak' and 'few' have no benchmark.

contract.note: Plain reading (paid demand limited relative to compute, and concentrated buyers) is ordinary. The Q4 2025 period is evaluator-selected but reasonable. Separating intermediaries from end users is fair.

evidence.note: CoreWeave 10-Q: about 67% of Q3 2025 revenue came from Microsoft. Shows concentration at one provider in an earlier quarter, not market-wide.
CBRE: record 2025 absorption, 1.4% vacancy, rising rents. Cuts against weak demand, but it measures general data-center leasing over a full year, not AI services demand in Q4.
Menlo survey: enterprise generative-AI spend tripled to $37B in 2025, across many products. Cuts against weak/concentrated demand, but it is an annual estimate, not a Q4 measure of compute use.

reviews.rationale: No representative Q4 2025 measure of AI compute capacity, paid utilization and buyer concentration is in the packet. CBRE and Menlo point against weak demand, but they use different metrics and periods. CoreWeave shows concentration at one firm only. The evidence does not settle the claim.

attribution.note: Zitron's own assertion in his own post.

semantics.note: Firm present-tense claim that NVIDIA earns hundreds of billions on uninstalled chips. The 'scandal' framing is rhetorical, but the core claim is factual. No period is stated.

contract.note: Reading 'hundreds of billions' as at least $200B is ordinary. Pairing a quarterly reference period with a flow metric is awkward: one quarter's revenue could never reach $200B. The contract avoids applying that against the speaker by leaving accumulation dates open. The accounting basis is unknown.

evidence.note: NVIDIA's FY2026 results: $215.9B total revenue (company disclosure). Total revenue says nothing about what share came from uninstalled chips.
NVIDIA blog, Oct 2025: Azure cluster with over 4,600 GB300 GPUs. One installation example; it predates the reference quarter and gives no aggregate revenue measure.

reviews.rationale: No reconciliation of NVIDIA chip revenue against customers' installation or inventory status is in the packet. Total revenue cannot stand in for revenue from uninstalled chips. One deployment example cannot bound the aggregate. The evidence neither supports nor contradicts the claim.
